# dependency-injector

> A high-performance, lock-free dependency injection container for Rust.

dependency-injector provides a thread-safe, type-safe DI container built on DashMap for concurrent access without mutex contention. It supports multiple service lifetimes (singleton, transient, lazy), scoped child containers with inheritance and overrides, compile-time injection via derive macros, structured logging, and FFI bindings for use from Go, Python, Node.js, C#, and C/C++. Benchmarks show singleton resolution in 17-32 ns, making it 6-14x faster than popular DI libraries in other languages.

## Links

- [Documentation](https://quinnjr.github.io/dependency-injector/)
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/quinnjr/dependency-injector)
- [Crates.io Package](https://crates.io/crates/dependency-injector)
- [API Docs (docs.rs)](https://docs.rs/dependency-injector)

## Key Features

- Lock-free performance -- built on DashMap for concurrent access without mutex contention
- Thread-safe -- safe to use across threads with `Arc<Container>`
- Type-safe -- compile-time guarantees with Rust's type system
- Multiple lifetimes -- singleton, transient, and lazy initialization
- Scoped containers -- create child containers with inherited and overridden services
- Zero config -- no macros required, just plain Rust (macros available optionally)
- Compile-time injection -- `#[derive(Inject)]` macro for automatic dependency resolution
- Structured logging -- JSON and pretty logging output via tracing
- FFI bindings -- use from Go, Python, Node.js, C#, and C/C++
- Framework integration -- works with the Armature HTTP framework
- Fuzz testing -- comprehensive fuzz targets for container operations

## Installation

```toml
[dependencies]
dependency-injector = "0.2"
```

## Quick Start

```rust
use dependency_injector::Container;

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Database { url: String }

#[derive(Clone)]
struct UserService { db: Database }

fn main() {
    let container = Container::new();

    // Register a singleton
    container.singleton(Database {
        url: "postgres://localhost/mydb".into(),
    });

    // Register with lazy initialization
    let c = container.clone();
    container.lazy(move || UserService {
        db: c.get().unwrap(),
    });

    // Resolve services
    let db = container.get::<Database>().unwrap();
    let users = container.get::<UserService>().unwrap();
    println!("Connected to: {}", db.url);
}
```
